brief: The census cannot see winter, and it has been telling the manager the map is flat for 16 iterations partly because of it. #181 added ICE, the 19th tile kind, and `census.mjs` reported unchanged in EVERY field. The cause is deliberate and documented in census.mjs's own comment: all three AGES sit at warmth 0.6929 so that the age axis measures age (the #14 fix), which means no seasonal state exists in any of the nine cells. Give the gate a winter reading. The existing 3 seeds x 3 ages must stay BIT-IDENTICAL and comparable — the baseline travels with the ladder, and breaking that throws away every census row in RUNLOG — so this is an ADDITION, not a re-cut of the ladder. Prove it the way a gate must be proved: pin a 'before' to the REF at #181's commit and show the new reading MOVES across it while the old nine cells do not. Fold in c266 while you are here: seed-identity pins five instants at seed 42 and 125/128 are wet, i.e. seed 42 gets ONE shower in 800 sim s, so its second seed should be chosen FOR its weather and the choice written down.
successLooksLike: `node census.mjs` prints a winter reading beside the summer one; run against the tree at #181 it shows ICE non-zero and tileKinds moving, where the current gate shows nothing. The nine existing cells are byte-identical to today's `census-latest.json`. The ledger says in one line whether `stall.mjs`'s mapFlat now reads the new fields or still cannot.
avoid: Do not change SEEDS or the three AGES, and do not re-pin the baseline in a way that makes today's rows incomparable. Do not turn this into a general census rewrite — one axis, proved against one ref.
